concept.name: Novation
concept.definition: The legal substitution, upon clearing, of the original contract between buyer and seller with two new contracts in which the central counterparty becomes the buyer to the seller and the seller to the buyer. Novation replaces mutual counterparty exposure among traders with exposure to the clearinghouse.
concept.intuition: Once your trade clears, the person on the other side legally disappears — your contract is now with the clearinghouse, and so is theirs.
concept.mechanics: When a trade is accepted for clearing, the clearing organization discharges the original bilateral contract and creates matched contracts with itself as central counterparty; this enables multilateral netting and lets either party exit by offsetting, regardless of the original counterparty's identity.
concept.failure_modes: Novation centralizes credit risk in the CCP, so its benefit depends entirely on the CCP's risk management; in legal disputes, whether and when novation occurred (trade acceptance timing) can determine who bears a default.
concept.misconceptions: Novation does not make markets risk-free — it substitutes a single, well-collateralized counterparty for many bilateral ones — and uncleared (bilateral) trades never receive this substitution.
concept.example: Two CME clearing members execute a Eurodollar futures trade with each other; upon clearing, CME Clearing becomes the seller to the buyer and the buyer to the seller, and the members no longer bear each other's credit risk.
